result.rationale: The diff adds a token refresh inside the SalesforceCalendarService constructor path (the `const response = await fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token"...)` block) with no expiry/validity gate, whereas the other services only refresh within an expired-token error handler. This runs an OAuth call plus a `prisma.credential.update` on every service instantiation, and a transient failure now rejects the whole connection even with a valid stored token. Verifiable directly from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs a refresh-token request and DB update unconditionally during connection setup: it calls `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)`, throws on non-OK (`if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...`), and then `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning `new jsforce.Connection(...)`. There is no expiry/validity check around the existing access token, so every time this connection-setup path runs it will trigger an OAuth call and write, and transient network/API errors will now prevent constructing the service even if the stored token is still valid.
